items.title: Armed Police Force AIG Banshiraj Dahal dismissed
items.desc: An investigation found that Dahal had acted in breach of conduct rules after he allegedly visited former chief justice Cholendra Shumsher Rana without authorisation.

items.title: Storms and heavy rain devastate crops across western Nepal
items.desc: Farmers in Kailali, Bardiya, Salyan and Dang have suffered losses to paddy, fruits, and vegetables, raising fears of lower yields and increasing demands for government relief.

items.title: Oman’s win over Canada gives Nepal a boost in League 2 race
items.desc: Oman beat Canada by 41 runs in Muscat, easing Nepal’s battle for a top-six finish in the ICC Cricket World Cup League 2.

items.title: Indian youth leader says protest will go ahead despite detentions
items.desc: Abhijeet Dipke vows to march in New Delhi despite reported detentions of thousands of supporters over a voter-list revision that opposition parties say has disenfranchised millions.

items.title: Thousands of flood-displaced children remain out of reach of measles vaccination
items.desc: Health officials have indefinitely stalled vaccination in three flood-hit districts, warning that displaced children face a heightened risk of infectious disease outbreaks.

items.title: Inside the deadlock at the world’s top climate science body
items.desc: The UN Environment Programme has said repeatedly that global efforts to limit warming are falling short and that faster emissions cuts are needed to avoid more extreme weather and climate-related disasters.

items.title: Road subsidence halts traffic on Prithvi Highway near Gajuri
items.desc: A nearly 100-metre stretch of road has developed cracks, while a 20-metre section has subsided, raising fears of further damage and landslides.

items.title: Houthi strikes on Riyadh airport killed three Saudis as war escalates
items.desc: The attacks disrupted flights to the Saudi capital as Riyadh intensified airstrikes in Yemen and the Houthis threatened further strikes on Saudi airspace and oil facilities.

items.title: From Pashupatinath offerings to supermarket tills, Indian tourists go cashless in Nepal
items.desc: UPI-powered QR payments are making it easier for Indian visitors to spend at religious sites, restaurants, supermarkets, resorts and nightlife venues across Nepal.

items.title: Chepang children risk swollen rivers to get to school
items.desc: With no bridge over the Lothar Khola, students and residents of four wards in Makwanpur’s Raksirang rural municipality face dangerous crossings and months of disrupted transport every monsoon.

items.title: Koshi police to deploy over 8,000 personnel for festival security
items.desc: Police will step up patrols, traffic checks and surveillance across all 14 districts.

items.title: Malaysia to raise minimum monthly wage to 2,000 ringgit
items.desc: The increase, announced in the 2027 budget, is expected to benefit more than four million workers, including Nepalis, although micro, small and medium-sized businesses will receive an exemption.

items.title: Navanethem “Navi” Pillay wins 2026 Nobel Peace Prize
items.desc: The peace prize is the ​fifth Nobel awarded this week, ​after literature, chemistry, physics and medicine. Venezuelan opposition leader Maria Corina Machado won in 2025.

items.title: Plane damaged at Riyadh airport as Houthis escalate attacks, sources say
items.desc: The Houthis say they are targeting the kingdom over its support for government forces in Yemen’s reignited civil war.

items.title: Why India’s tens of millions of voter deletions have led to widespread protests
items.desc: Election Commission data cited by Modi’s Bharatiya Janata Party shows about 130 million names, more than the population of Japan, have been deleted from ‌electoral rolls during the verification exercise.

items.title: Dashain rush brings Dhankuta’s weekly markets to life
items.desc: Farmers are selling livestock to cover festival expenses, while traders see rising demand for clothes, food and household essentials.

items.title: Zelenskiy accuses US of inaction as Russian strikes kill over 70 in two days
items.desc: Hours after the strike on the embattled city of Kramatorsk tore through two buses, Zelenskiy criticised Washington’s effort to pursue economic ties with Russia while also seeking to mediate the more than four-year war.

items.title: Dashain dakshina arrives with a phone notification
items.desc: More Nepalis are sending and receiving festival money through digital wallets, mobile banking and QR codes, even as cash remains part of the Tika ritual.

items.title: Sixth insurance-related case filed against Deepak Bhatta and 17 others
items.desc: The latest charges allege that funds were siphoned from Himalayan Re-Insurance through a series of transactions, with earlier money laundering and insurance-related cases still pending.

items.title: Storms and heavy rain destroy crops just before harvest
items.desc: Farmers in Kailali, Bardiya, Salyan and Dang have suffered losses to paddy, fruit and vegetables, raising fears of lower yields and increasing demands for government relief.

items.title: Probe recommends action against suspended APF chief Dahal
items.desc: An investigation report concludes that Additional Inspector General Banshiraj Dahal violated the force’s code of conduct and recommends disciplinary action under the APF Regulations, 2015.

items.title: Bus ticket bookings open ahead of festival rush
items.desc: Passengers can buy tickets at major bus stations or through online platforms as transport operators prepare for the annual homecoming rush.

items.title: Sacred Splendor brings the Valley’s living heritage under one roof
items.desc: Curated by Pradip Shakya, the exhibition places Hindu and Buddhist imagery side by side.

items.title: At least five killed in Pokhara school bus crash
items.desc: Four students and a parent who hitched a ride on the bus died after it plunged 150 to 200 metres down a slope. Rescue teams are searching for survivors.

items.title: Nepali Congress voting begins after delays
items.desc: Bad weather and ballot-paper printing delays pushed polling back by a day, with 7,317 delegates eligible to vote.

items.title: US freezes green card route for Microsoft, Infosys, Tata; Vance says ‘visa fraud’
items.desc: The US move bars major tech and IT outsourcing firms from sponsoring foreign workers for green cards amid a Trump administration crackdown on alleged visa fraud and claims of job losses for American workers.

items.title: A Nepali photographer rediscovers Calcutta after decades
items.desc: In its streets, riverbanks and neighbourhoods, old traditions meet the restless energy of everyday life.

items.title: Tribhuvan University to distribute question papers online, publish results within 60 days
items.desc: The university has at times taken over a year to publish results and these delays can force students to postpone further studies for an entire year or miss job opportunities.

items.title: Congress leadership vote postponed again, set for Friday
items.desc: A crowded field and late finalisation of candidate list delayed ballot printing and frustrated delegates eager to return to home districts for Dashain.
